drhp.business: Ram Ratna Wires, operating since 1992, manufactures copper and aluminium winding wires and strips across one of the industry's widest dimensional ranges (from 5 mm down to ultra-fine 0.016 mm), serving India's electrical ecosystem. It has expanded beyond winding wires into specialised conductors, value-added electrical solutions and seamless copper tubes (via the Bhiwadi facility and merged Global Copper), positioning itself as an integrated copper products platform. risks.note: Efficient use of raw materials, particularly copper, is critical for the resource-intensive winding-wire and copper-tube operations; inefficient consumption directly erodes margins and strains supply resilience.
risks.risk: Copper raw-material intensity and price volatility

risks.note: Energy consumption remains a major driver of manufacturing costs, and efficiency investments are needed to stay aligned with evolving environmental regulations and climate commitments.
Manufacturing operations inherently carry workplace risks; strong safety systems are essential for workforce protection and statutory compliance, with failures risking legal and financial penalties.
risks.risk: Occupational health and safety in manufacturing

risks.note: The supply chain is a significant source of indirect environmental and social impact; vendor failure to adhere to ESG standards can cause supply disruptions, reputational damage, and financial penalties.
Operations are subject to varied environmental, labour and corporate regulations; lapses can cause business disruptions and fines, requiring proactive compliance monitoring.
risks.risk: Regulatory compliance across environmental, labour and corporate rules

risks.note: Exposure to demand fluctuations and geographic-sector concentration; the Company pursues market diversification across geographies and sectors (EV, renewable energy) and export expansion to reduce this risk.

Reliance on commoditised wire products invites competitive pressure; a strategic shift toward higher-margin value-added products (paper magnet wires, ultrafine copper wires) is being pursued to defend profitability.
risks.risk: Commoditisation and margin pressure in standard products

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).

sk.structure: DG sets classified by capacity: LHP (7.5-160 kVA), MHP (180-500 kVA), HHP (>500 kVA); MSLG sets 3-10 MW for continuous/base-load. Wind potential concentrated in five states: Rajasthan (24%), Gujarat (16%), Maharashtra (15%), Karnataka (15%), Andhra Pradesh (11%).
